access.fees: No wilderness entry fee. The developed Harts Pass Trailhead (vault toilet) may require a Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass for parking; the more rustic Slate Peak/Slate Pass and Monument Creek trailheads typically aren't fee sites, but carrying a pass is a safe bet.
access.rules: Standard Pasayten Wilderness group-size limits apply; use bear-resistant food storage given the 2024-approved North Cascades grizzly bear reintroduction effort, which covers the Pasayten.
access.permit: Free, non-quota, self-issued wilderness permit at the trailhead — no reservation or quota system for the Pasayten Wilderness.
access.closures: Harts Pass Road (FR 5400) — the primary access road for all standard approaches — was closed indefinitely by the Forest Service in spring 2026 after storm damage; the Forest Service's Methow Valley road-status table lists it open again as of July 2, 2026. Separately, the Ptarmigan Fire closure (Forest Service order 06-17-04-26-39, in effect September 9 through October 31, 2026) closes the Buckskin Ridge (#498), West Fork Pasayten (#472), Eureka Creek (#474) and Shellrock (#484.1) trails and the Monument Creek Trail (#484) north of the Lake of the Woods turnoff, which cuts off both standard approaches. Methow Valley Ranger District, (509) 996-4000.
access.parking_pass: Northwest Forest Pass required at trailheads (e.g. Andrews Creek, Chewuch River) — $5/day or $30/annual.

overnight_permit.where: Fill one out at the trailhead registration box. No reservation is needed.

before.beta: From Upper Royal Basin, ascend heather/talus to the moraine rim, drop to snowfields and climb to the ~6,900 ft col between Clark and Mount Johnson. From the col, ascend talus to the cliff base and skirt right on a wide, low-angle (Class 2) southwest-facing ledge — exposed-looking but easy. Where the cliffs split into a Y-shaped gully, go straight up to a boulder then right to a notch on the SE ridge (Class 2-3), descend the ridge to an east ledge via a diagonal crack system (Class 2-3, exposed but solid), follow the ledge north, then climb a loose gully (Class 3) to a dihedral ramp (Class 4, or a Class 3 broken face alternative on the left) and finally a shallow slot through the north face of the summit block (Class 3-4, good holds). Descend by reversing the route with one short rappel off the summit block. Route-finding is the main difficulty; published descriptions are described by multiple parties as sketchy, and several climbers have produced their own route sketches after the fact.
hazards: long, complex approach (roughly 14-16 mi round trip to Upper Royal Basin plus off-trail talus/scree to Surprise Col)
sustained loose rock ('choss') in the corkscrew route's gullies
exposed Class 3-4 downclimb of a diagonal crack that looks like a cliff-out from above -- watch for the cairn marking its top
a roughly 60-ft rappel is often needed off the summit block
lingering snow on the approach and in upper gullies into July
difficult, easy-to-lose route-finding around the summit block
black bear activity in Royal Basin (bear canister required)
no cell service; a rescue would involve a long multi-mile carry-out

pitch_detail.notes: From Upper Royal Basin, ascend heather and talus to the glacial moraine rim, then drop to snowfields and climb to the ~6,900-6,920 ft col between Mount Clark and Mount Johnson (Surprise Col).
From the col, ascend a talus slope to the base of the cliffs, then skirt right beneath the cliffs on a wide, southwest-facing ledge for roughly 100 yards — looks exposed but is easy.
Where the cliffs split into a Y-shaped gully system, climb straight up to a large boulder, then veer right to gain a notch on the southeast ridge.
Descend the southeast ridge to an east-facing ledge via a diagonal crack system — exposed but on solid rock.
Follow the east ledge northward for roughly 50 yards.
Ascend a shallow, loose/rubbly gully to the base of a dihedral ramp.
Climb the steeply inclined dihedral ramp direct (Class 4), or scramble a broken face on the left as an easier alternative (Class 3).
Ascend a shallow slot through the north face of the summit block to the top — described as "fun" with good holds.
Roughly 60 ft rappel off the summit block, then downclimb the slot and reverse the route back to the col.
